patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension and chronic atrial fibrillation on warfarin who joins in 2020. Over six years he has diabetic polyneuropathy, a nasal basal cell carcinoma, a pharyngoesophageal diverticulum, endophthalmitis after cataract surgery, a venous air embolism at angiography, a diabetic foot osteomyelitis, an appendiceal abscess and finally a locally advanced mucin-producing pancreatic adenocarcinoma with chronic DIC.

documents.body:
66 y/o retired construction foreman transferring care from his former primary care office.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes since about 2006, on metformin the whole time, no hypoglycemia. Hypertension about as long, on lisinopril and HCTZ. Atrial fibrillation picked up at his old practice around 2016; has been on warfarin since, INR drawn monthly there. No palpitations he notices, no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no bleeding.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, chronic atrial fibrillation.
PSH: tonsils and adenoids out at age 7.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (adjusted to INR), atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: father had type 2 diabetes and an MI at 72. Mother hypertension and a basal cell skin cancer. An uncle on his father's side had pancreatic cancer.
Social: smoked about a pack a day for 20 years, stopped in 2016. A drink or two a week, socially. Retired foreman, ran residential framing crews for decades.

Exam: well-appearing, comfortable. Vitals as charted. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses present, monofilament sensation intact today.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes - A1c sent. Continue metformin.
2. Hypertension - at goal, continue lisinopril/HCTZ. BMP today.
3. Chronic AF on warfarin - CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age, HTN, DM). We will manage INR here; RN to set him up with monthly checks, goal 2-3. INR today.
4. Lipids - on atorvastatin 40, lipid panel today.
5. Health maintenance - will request old records including colonoscopy. Flu shot and Tdap at a nurse visit next month.

RTC 3 months.

Outside dermatology group
Date of service: 12/13/2021
Re: Eugene Connolly, DOB 09/09/1954

Thank you for referring Mr. Connolly, a 67-year-old with diabetes, for a nasal lesion. He reports a bump on the nose for about a year that bleeds now and then when he shaves and is otherwise without symptoms.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin, capsaicin cream. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam: On the lateral aspect of the nose there is a 1.5 cm pearly, flesh-colored nodule with overlying telangiectasias and a central depression. No cervical, preauricular or submandibular lymphadenopathy. Remainder of the face, scalp, neck, arms and trunk examined without other suspicious lesions.

Procedure: After consent and local anesthesia, a shave biopsy was taken. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Warfarin continued.

Impression: clinically a basal cell carcinoma; pathology pending. Given the location, margin-controlled excision would be recommended if confirmed. We will call him with results.

conditions.label: Basal cell carcinoma of skin of nose

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Skin, lateral nose, shave biopsy.
MICROSCOPIC: Nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact arising from the epidermis and extending into the dermis.
DIAGNOSIS: Basal cell carcinoma, nodular type. Tumor extends to the deep and peripheral margins of the specimen.
reports.conclusion: Basal cell carcinoma, nodular type, lateral nose.

Reason for referral: dysphagia.

History: Mr. Connolly describes six months of steadily worsening difficulty getting both solids and liquids down. He has nighttime regurgitation of food that is clearly undigested, which sets off coughing spells. He is also bothered by halitosis despite careful oral hygiene. He has diabetes with neuropathy, hypertension, and atrial fibrillation on warfarin; a nasal basal cell carcinoma was excised in January.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: Well appearing. In the left side of the neck there is a small, soft, non-tender fullness that gurgles when pressed. No lymphadenopathy. Abdomen benign.

Barium swallow (today): saccular pouch off the posterior hypopharyngeal wall.

Assessment: Zenker (pharyngoesophageal) diverticulum, symptomatic.
Plan: Referral to ENT to discuss transoral endoscopic versus open repair. Upper endoscopy not needed before that consultation. Soft diet, small bites, remain upright after eating.

Thank you for this referral.

Regional hospital emergency department - ophthalmology on call
Visit 01/25/2023
Patient: Eugene Connolly, 68-year-old man

CC: right eye pain, vision worse x2 days.

HPI: Four weeks after uncomplicated right cataract surgery. Two days ago the right eye became suddenly painful with blurred vision, and both have steadily worsened. Has diabetes (with foot neuropathy), past nasal skin cancer and a swallowing pouch treated last year.

Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, warfarin, atorvastatin. Allergies: none known.

Exam: Right upper lid swollen. Conjunctiva diffusely injected. Slit lamp: corneal edema, hypopyon, marked anterior chamber and vitreous inflammation. VA right hand motions, left 20/30. Fundus view poor through the corneal edema. B-scan: vitreous opacities, retina attached.

Assessment: acute postoperative endophthalmitis, right eye.

Treatment: vitreous tap with intravitreal vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL and ceftazidime 2.25 mg/0.1 mL. Sample to microbiology. Moxifloxacin drops four times daily and prednisolone acetate 1% hourly while awake. Warfarin continued.
Follow-up: retina clinic in 48 hours.

Addendum 01/28: vitreous culture growing coagulase-negative staphylococci, covered by intravitreal vancomycin.

Regional hospital - medicine service
Admitted 06/28/2024 via the emergency department. Discharged 07/03/2024.

Reason for admission: left foot ulcer, 3 weeks, not healing.

History: 69-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for about 18 years and diabetic neuropathy. The ulcer started as a blister from a new pair of shoes and has grown larger and deeper. No fever or chills. More redness lately and a bad smell from the wound. Also hypertension, chronic AF on warfarin, prior nasal BCC, pharyngeal pouch repair, right cataract surgery with endophthalmitis, normal coronary angiogram 12/2023.
Home meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Exam on arrival: afebrile. Left foot ulcer 3 cm across with a purulent base and surrounding erythema; no crepitus. Light touch diminished in both feet. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses weak on both sides.
Labs: WBC 14.0, hemoglobin A1c 9.2%, ESR 70 mm/hr, CRP 15 mg/dL. INR 2.4.
Imaging: foot X-ray with cortical erosion next to the ulcer. ABI 0.98 right, 0.96 left.

Diagnosis: diabetic foot infection with osteomyelitis, left foot.

Hospital course: Started on IV vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Podiatric surgery performed debridement of the ulcer and underlying bone with bone biopsy on 06/30 (warfarin held beforehand). Bone culture grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus; antibiotics narrowed to cefazolin. PICC placed 07/02. Blood sugars managed with correction insulin while inpatient; metformin resumed. Warfarin resumed 07/01.

Discharge medications: cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours via home infusion through 08/11/2024 (6 weeks); continue home medications unchanged.
Wound care: daily dressing per home nursing; offloading boot, no bare-foot walking.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week; infectious disease in 6 weeks; podiatry in 1 week. INR weekly while on cefazolin (may raise INR).

Outside medical oncology practice
Date of visit: 01/14/2026
Re: Eugene Connolly, DOB 09/09/1954

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Connolly with a newly diagnosed pancreatic head adenocarcinoma.

History: three months of epigastric pain, poor appetite and weight loss, then jaundice. CA 19-9 150. CT 1/6: 3.2 cm head mass encasing the SMA beyond 180 degrees, no liver lesions, no ascites; chest CT clear. EUS-FNA 1/9: mucin-producing adenocarcinoma; covered metal biliary stent placed. Jaundice improving since the stent.
PMH: type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, hypertension, chronic AF on warfarin, past nodular BCC of the nose, pharyngoesophageal diverticulum (stapled 2022), right cataract surgery with endophthalmitis 2023, foot osteomyelitis 2024, appendectomy 12/2024. Normal coronary angiogram 2023.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, warfarin 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, capsaicin cream. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: paternal uncle with pancreatic cancer.
Performance status ECOG 1. Weight 77 kg.

Labs today: platelets 104, hemoglobin 11.6, fibrinogen 148 mg/dL, D-dimer 5.6 ug/mL FEU, INR 1.7 (warfarin restarted 1/10 after the procedure), total bilirubin 1.8.

Assessment:
1. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, mucin-producing, head, locally advanced and unresectable (arterial encasement), no distant disease on imaging.
2. Chronic (compensated) disseminated intravascular coagulation related to the mucinous adenocarcinoma - low platelets and fibrinogen with raised D-dimer, no bleeding.
3. Chronic AF requiring anticoagulation.

Plan:
- Gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel, days 1, 8 and 15 of 28-day cycles, starting 1/26.
- Anticoagulation: stop warfarin today; start enoxaparin 80 mg subcutaneously every 12 hours, which covers his AF and is preferred over warfarin with cancer-associated DIC. Teaching done in clinic.
- CA 19-9 and coagulation labs each cycle. Restaging CT after 2-3 cycles.
We will keep you updated. Please continue to manage his diabetes and blood pressure.
